US claims that almost 9m b/d of oil is leaving via the Strait of Hormuz (not counting bypass pipelines) on a 7-day average. That's well above what most tanker trackers have currently (4m-6m b/d).

After a brief hiatus, Ukraine has steeped up its attacks against Russian oil refineries, hitting four plants in two days (plus another five last week). The latest attacks have hit plants more than 2,000 kilometres from the Ukrainian border.

US President Donald Trump seems to be pursuing a “no war, no peace — just economic pressure” on Iran. 

Key for that strategy is to get enough oil out of the Strait of Hormuz in ‘dark shuttles’ so prices don’t spiral out of control before the economic pain on Tehran works. Key problem? Iran has demonstrated an incredible capacity to absorb financial pain in the past.

Regular followers of our Hormuz flow updates will note that I've shifted this graphic to a 7dma from our normal 10dma to be directly comparable to Secretary Wright's estimate.

The 10dma peaks out at ~6 MMbpd rather than ~7 MMbpd.

Confirmed shipments down sharply over the past week, both in Hormuz and in the Red Sea, but in both instances I think it's likely an undercount that will be revised higher as more dark transits are confirmed (plenty currently suspected)

EXCLUSIVE: The 28-year-old Suezmax tanker CARUZO (IMO 9137648), which is under UK, EU, New Zealand, Canadian, Swiss, and Australian sanctions (but not US sanctions), sailed past us in Istanbul carrying one million barrels of Russian crude oil.

The first thing we noticed was that the crew had covered the superstructure with netting and boxed themselves in, apparently out of fear of Ukrainian drone strikes. The aft half of the vessel also appears to have additional protection in the form of cages dangling off the sides, intended to guard the engine room against attacks by sea drones.

The fear is real.
